paragraphs: Training with incorrect labels creates a problem for the loss function: it needs to guide learning without encouraging the network to absorb every labeling mistake. Some robust approaches use Mean Absolute Error, or MAE, as a component. The paper identifies a drawback of this choice: treating samples equally can slow convergence and make optimization difficult.

The authors introduce Normalized Negative Loss Functions, a class of passive losses with theoretical robustness properties. These losses put greater emphasis on clean samples that the model has already memorized. They then replace the MAE component in the existing Active Passive Loss framework with these new losses, producing a framework called Active Negative Loss.

Experiments on benchmark and real-world datasets show that losses constructed through this framework can outperform state-of-the-art methods. The contribution is therefore both a new family of robust losses and a way to incorporate them into an established approach. The findings support reconsidering how a robust loss distributes attention across training examples, rather than treating equal weighting as the default.
neurips-2023-active-negative-loss-functi.tldr: Active Negative Loss replaces MAE with robust losses that emphasize memorized clean samples and can improve learning with noisy labels.

paragraphs: Research on 3D-aware image generation often combines several architectural choices and training techniques. When a complete system works well, that mixture makes it difficult to determine which parts deserve credit. This paper addresses the problem by organizing the generation process into independently replaceable modules within a shared codebase.

The codebase follows an established approach that places a neural radiance field inside a generative adversarial network’s generator. Its modular structure lets researchers develop individual components and compare alternatives within a common implementation. Reproducing a range of leading algorithms demonstrates that the framework can accommodate existing methods, making it useful for examining component contributions across systems.

The authors also analyze different point-feature representations, the role of the generator’s final upsampler, and dependence on assumptions about camera poses. These investigations aim to clarify how existing systems work and identify research directions. The abstract does not state a preferred choice for each component; its central contribution is a practical basis for more controlled comparisons and deeper analysis.
neurips-2023-benchmarking-and-analyzing-.tldr: A modular codebase makes 3D-aware image generators easier to reproduce, compare, and analyze component by component.

paragraphs: Compositional generalization concerns learning reusable parts and applying them in combinations beyond those encountered during training. Although people routinely benefit from this ability, machine-learning models can struggle even when their designs explicitly encourage composition. This paper asks what conditions can actually support such generalization, approaching the question through the mechanism that produces observations.

The authors treat compositionality as a property of the data-generating process. Inspired by identifiable representation learning, this perspective shifts attention from whether examples appear compositional to whether the underlying process has a recoverable compositional structure. They derive sufficient conditions involving the support of the training distribution—the cases it can contain—and the model architecture.

The conditions are described as mild, and the authors demonstrate applications of the framework to real-world scenarios alongside empirical validation. Their result establishes circumstances under which compositional generalization is supported by theory. Because the conditions are sufficient, the claim does not imply that every successful model must satisfy them. The broader contribution is a foundation for reasoning about composition through explicit assumptions.
neurips-2023-compositional-generalizatio.tldr: The paper derives sufficient conditions for compositional generalization by studying the structure of the data-generating process.

paragraphs: An information seller must decide both what to reveal and what to charge. Buyers value information according to how it improves their decisions, so the same information can have different values for different buyers. With multiple buyers, its value can also depend on what other people learn. This makes market design a problem of shaping information as well as pricing it.

The paper introduces a deep-learning framework for designing such markets to maximize expected revenue. It learns signaling schemes: statistical procedures that reveal selected information. Beyond incentives governing buyers’ bids, the framework handles obedience constraints arising from their downstream actions. These requirements distinguish the problem from learning auction rules that allocate goods.

Experiments show that the framework can reproduce known theoretical solutions almost precisely and extend to more complex settings. The authors also use it to establish the optimality of new market designs and develop conjectures about their structure. Its significance is as both a design tool and a means of investigating economic questions about selling decision-relevant information.
neurips-2023-data-market-design-through-.tldr: A deep-learning framework learns what information to sell and at what price while accounting for buyers’ incentives and decisions.

paragraphs: Gradient-based optimization often requires choosing parameters carefully to obtain good convergence. DoWG, short for Distance over Weighted Gradients, is designed to remove that tuning requirement. The paper presents an easy-to-implement optimizer and analyzes whether it can achieve rates comparable to gradient descent whose parameters have already been optimally chosen.

Its key mechanism changes how past gradients are accumulated. Algorithms in the AdaGrad family commonly maintain a running average of squared gradients. DoWG uses a distance-based weighting of that history. The authors identify this weighting as essential to obtaining both efficient convergence and automatic adaptation to smooth and nonsmooth optimization problems.

For convex optimization, the paper proves that DoWG matches the convergence rate of optimally tuned gradient descent up to a logarithmic factor, without parameter tuning. Practical machine-learning experiments complement this guarantee and show training behavior described as operating at the edge of stability. The theoretical claim is specifically about convex problems, while the experiments provide separate evidence of practical usefulness.
neurips-2023-dowg-unleashed-an-efficient.tldr: DoWG uses distance-weighted gradient history to avoid tuning while nearly matching optimally tuned gradient descent’s convex convergence rate.

paragraphs: Activation functions affect how neural networks learn, but designing them by hand is difficult and searching through candidates can be expensive. This paper develops a way to predict which functions are promising, supported by benchmarks built from training convolutional networks, residual networks, and vision transformers with 2,913 systematically generated activation functions.

Analysis of these benchmarks identifies two useful predictors of performance: the spectrum of the Fisher information matrix associated with the network’s predictions at initialization, and the activation function’s output distribution. The authors use these signals to construct a surrogate model. This model guides optimization by estimating the promise of activation choices rather than relying only on full training evaluations.

Applied to several real-world tasks, the approach discovers improved activation functions, including a sigmoidal design that outperforms the other functions considered. That result challenges the assumption that rectifier-style nonlinearities should always be preferred. The contribution combines reusable benchmark data, evidence about predictive characteristics, and a search method for finding better activations in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-efficient-activation-functi.tldr: A surrogate model uses initialization-time signals to guide activation-function search and discovers strong alternatives to rectifier nonlinearities.

paragraphs: In exemplar-free class-incremental learning, a model must learn new classes without replaying examples from earlier tasks. One strategy freezes the feature extractor after the first task and updates only the classifier. FeCAM examines classifiers that represent each class with a prototype and assign examples according to their distance from those prototypes.

The authors find that ordinary Euclidean distance works well for jointly trained features but is suboptimal when data changes over successive learning stages. Different classes have differently shaped feature distributions. FeCAM revisits Mahalanobis distance, which accounts for covariance relationships between features, so classification can reflect these unequal shapes instead of relying on a uniform distance measure.

Experiments indicate that modeling covariance is better than earlier approaches that sample features from normal distributions and train a linear classifier. The method supports both many-example and few-example class-incremental settings, as well as domain-incremental learning. It achieves state-of-the-art results on several standard benchmarks without updating the backbone, showing the practical importance of the classifier’s treatment of feature geometry.
neurips-2023-fecam-exploiting-the-hetero.tldr: FeCAM improves exemplar-free continual learning by using covariance-aware distances to account for differently shaped class distributions.

paragraphs: Federated training becomes harder when only some clients participate in each round, their data differs, and gradients can grow sharply. This paper studies these issues together under relaxed smoothness: the gradient’s rate of change can scale with its magnitude. The setting is motivated by loss functions of certain neural networks, including recurrent networks with potentially exploding gradients.

The proposed algorithm, EPISODE++, keeps historical statistics for each client. It uses them to construct correction terms called control variates and to decide how to clip updates from currently sampled clients. The analysis proves linear speedup with the number of participating clients, fewer communication rounds, and resilience to heterogeneous data within the studied setting.

A complementary lower bound shows why clipping alone is insufficient for a particular minibatch SGD setting with random client selection but no stochastic-gradient randomness. Its convergence still depends on a potentially large maximum gradient norm. Experiments training recurrent networks on federated text classification tasks show EPISODE++ outperforming strong baselines, connecting the theoretical motivation to practical training.
neurips-2023-federated-learning-with-cli.tldr: EPISODE++ uses client history to stabilize federated training with partial participation, heterogeneous data, and potentially unbounded smoothness.

paragraphs: Many self-supervised learning methods emphasize a representation of an entire image. Object detection and segmentation also need meaningful representations of the image’s local content. FLSL addresses this mismatch by making feature-level grouping central to self-supervised training, with the aim of learning representations better suited to identifying individual objects and regions.

The paper identifies an underlying mean-shift clustering process in vision transformers that aligns with image semantics. Building on this observation, FLSL uses a transformer to learn embeddings and clusters jointly. Its two-level clustering objectives draw on mean-shift and k-means perspectives, encouraging features to form semantic groups both within a view and across different views.

Experiments show improvements in object detection and instance segmentation on MS-COCO using vision-transformer backbones within Mask R-CNN. The method also outperforms existing self-supervised approaches on UAV object detection and video instance segmentation benchmarks. Together, these results support the value of aligning the structure of self-supervised learning with the local distinctions required by dense prediction tasks.
neurips-2023-flsl-feature-level-self-sup.tldr: FLSL trains vision transformers to cluster local features, improving self-supervised representations for detection and segmentation.

paragraphs: Style-based generators use modulation to capture differences between generated examples. However, ordinary convolution still processes features at fixed spatial locations, restricting how directly it can represent geometric variation. This paper adds a mechanism that lets the generator change where convolution operates according to the particular example being generated.

The proposed modulated transformation module predicts spatial offsets under the control of latent codes. Those offsets allow convolution to access variable locations for different instances. This gives the generator an additional way to express geometric deformation, complementing the variation already handled by style modulation. The module is designed to plug into existing GAN generators.

Experiments suggest that the approach transfers across image generation, 3D-aware image synthesis, and video generation, and works with leading frameworks without hyperparameter tuning. For human generation on TaiChi, it reduces StyleGAN3’s FID from 21.36 to 13.60. This concrete improvement supports the usefulness of learning spatial transformations, while the broader experiments indicate compatibility across the evaluated generation tasks.
neurips-2023-learning-modulated-transfor.tldr: A plug-in GAN module learns latent-controlled spatial offsets so convolution can better model geometric variation.

paragraphs: Imitation learning often assumes that demonstrations include the actions producing each observed change. In natural settings, those actions may be hidden, and behavior may depend on history beyond the current state. This paper addresses both issues by learning from state-only sequences within a non-Markovian decision-making framework.

The method uses a deep generative model of state transitions, with the policy represented as an energy-based prior over latent variables. Training uses maximum likelihood, combining short-run Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling from the prior with importance sampling for the posterior. This formulation makes learning a model of observed sequences the basis for acquiring decision-making behavior.

The resulting model links action selection and planning through inference. Model-free policy execution corresponds to sampling from the prior, while model-based planning corresponds to posterior sampling initialized from the policy. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness in path planning with non-Markovian constraints and strong performance on challenging MuJoCo domains. These results support learning useful decision processes without access to demonstrators’ action signals.
neurips-2023-learning-non-markovian-deci.tldr: A generative model learns history-dependent decision-making from state-only demonstrations and expresses policy execution and planning as sampling.

paragraphs: Chip floorplanning includes deciding where to place large components called macros. A useful placement avoids overlaps while reducing half-perimeter wirelength, or HPWL, the wiring objective considered in this paper. Finding such placements efficiently is an important design problem, previously approached with packing methods, analytical optimization, and reinforcement learning.

WireMask-BBO introduces a black-box optimization framework built around a wire-mask-guided greedy procedure for evaluating the objective. Different black-box optimizers can operate within this framework. Its design therefore connects a placement-specific evaluation procedure with a broader family of search algorithms, rather than tying the approach to a single optimizer.

Experiments show significantly shorter HPWL with substantially less running time than previous methods. The framework can also begin from an existing placement and improve it, with reported HPWL improvements of up to 50%. That figure describes the reported potential gain, not a guaranteed outcome for every placement. The results suggest value both for generating placements and for refining solutions already available in a design workflow.
neurips-2023-macro-placement-by-wire-mas.tldr: WireMask-BBO combines black-box search with a wire-guided evaluation procedure to improve macro placement speed and wirelength.

paragraphs: Learning related tasks together can be useful, but deciding what to do next also requires knowing how uncertain each prediction is. This paper develops confidence intervals for multitask regression in an agnostic setting where the learner lacks both task similarity information and task features. The intervals also do not require independent, identically distributed data.

The authors use these uncertainty bounds to analyze online learning. Their regret guarantees can improve substantially over learning tasks independently, depending on how similar the tasks are. They also propose an algorithm that adapts to this similarity without knowing its value beforehand. This connects the potential benefit of information sharing to an implementable learning procedure.

A second application considers active learning across several tasks when only one task can be queried for feedback each round. The proposed no-regret algorithm uses the confidence intervals to choose which task to query while pursuing all tasks simultaneously. Synthetic and drug-discovery experiments validate the bounds and algorithms, supporting uncertainty estimation as a tool for coordinating limited feedback across related problems.
neurips-2023-multitask-learning-with-no-.tldr: New multitask confidence bounds enable online and active-learning algorithms that adapt to unknown task similarity.

paragraphs: Functional brain imaging can be represented as a graph, with brain regions connected according to their interactions. However, choices about preprocessing and graph construction create a large design space. NeuroGraph provides a benchmark collection for investigating these choices and evaluating graph-based prediction of behavioral and cognitive traits.

The authors construct 35 datasets covering both static connectivity and connectivity that changes over time. They benchmark more than 15 baseline methods and provide general frameworks for learning from static and dynamic graphs. This breadth makes dataset construction itself part of the evaluation, allowing researchers to examine how representation choices relate to predictive performance.

Across their experiments, correlation vectors as node features, larger numbers of regions of interest, and sparser graphs are associated with improved performance. These are empirical findings from the studied settings rather than universal prescriptions for every neuroimaging task. An accompanying Python package brings together datasets, baseline implementations, training, and standardized evaluation, providing a shared basis for subsequent research in graph-based neuroimaging analysis.
neurips-2023-neurograph-benchmarks-for-g.tldr: NeuroGraph benchmarks brain-connectivity graph construction and learning methods across 35 datasets for behavioral and cognitive prediction.

paragraphs: Likelihood-based generative models are attractive because they can produce new data with a single model evaluation, but their sample quality often trails leading score-based diffusion models. This paper borrows data mollification, a smoothing idea associated with diffusion models, to improve how likelihood-based generators are optimized.

The authors interpret mollification as a continuation method. Training begins with an objective that is easier to optimize and gradually transitions toward the original target. The motivation includes improving density estimation in low-density regions and addressing manifold overfitting. This connects a change in the training data’s treatment to a smoother progression through the optimization problem.

The proposed modification can be added with one line in the optimization loop, and the authors report improved generation quality without computational overhead. Tests on real-world image datasets and UCI benchmarks include variants of variational autoencoders and normalizing flows, showing large improvements in FID and density estimation. The findings support a lightweight training change as a useful way to improve the evaluated likelihood-based models.
neurips-2023-one-line-of-code-data-molli.tldr: Gradually smoothing the training objective through data mollification improves tested likelihood-based generators with a one-line training change.

paragraphs: Widely spaced panoramic captures can reduce storage and bandwidth needs for virtual environments, but generating views between those captures is difficult. Sparse 360-degree images provide limited geometric evidence, and some scene regions appear in only one image. Existing radiance-field methods can consequently overfit the supplied views.

PanoGRF builds spherical radiance fields using information directly from panoramic images. For each sampled 3D point, it gathers geometry and appearance features through spherical projection. This avoids losing information by first converting panoramas into perspective images. The design makes the full panoramic representation part of the view-synthesis process rather than an input that must be reformatted.

To help with regions visible from only one viewpoint, PanoGRF incorporates monocular 360-degree depth priors into spherical depth estimation. These priors strengthen the geometry features where cross-view evidence is limited. Experiments on multiple panoramic datasets show significant improvements over leading generalizable view-synthesis methods developed for both panoramas and perspective images, supporting the value of combining panorama-native aggregation with depth information.
neurips-2023-panogrf-generalizable-spher.tldr: PanoGRF combines direct spherical feature aggregation with panoramic depth priors to improve view synthesis from widely spaced panoramas.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning algorithms often assume that feedback arrives immediately after an action. Delays complicate exploration because the agent must keep making decisions while some outcomes remain unknown. This paper studies delayed feedback with linear function approximation and develops posterior-sampling algorithms with theoretical regret guarantees.

The first algorithm, Delayed-PSVI, explores possible value functions through noise perturbations combined with posterior sampling. Its analysis handles unknown stochastic delays and yields a worst-case regret bound with an additive term proportional to expected delay. This explicitly captures the cost of waiting for observations within the studied setting, rather than treating feedback timing as irrelevant.

The second algorithm, Delayed-LPSVI, uses Langevin dynamics as a gradient-based approximate sampling procedure. It improves computational efficiency and extends applicability to high-dimensional problems while retaining the same order of regret guarantee. Empirical evaluations support the statistical and computational effectiveness of both algorithms. Together, the results connect uncertainty-driven exploration, delayed observations, and practical sampling costs within a single line of analysis.
neurips-2023-posterior-sampling-with-del.tldr: Two posterior-sampling algorithms provide regret guarantees for reinforcement learning with linear approximation and unknown stochastic feedback delays.

paragraphs: Queueing controllers must make decisions about systems whose parameters may initially be unknown. Learning those parameters can increase congestion before the controller settles into effective behavior. The paper argues that measures focused on eventual performance miss much of this early learning burden, even though that burden is central to the difficulty of operating under uncertainty.

The authors introduce Cost of Learning in Queueing, or CLQ. It measures the maximum increase in time-averaged queue length caused by parameter uncertainty. Focusing on this maximum captures the buildup associated with learning rather than only assessing how well an algorithm behaves after substantial experience.

The paper characterizes CLQ for a single queue with multiple servers, then extends the results to multiple queues, multiple servers, and queue networks. Its analysis combines Lyapunov methods with bandit-learning analysis and provides guarantees for a broad range of algorithms. The contribution is both a performance measure suited to learning-induced congestion and a common framework for studying it across different queueing structures.
neurips-2023-quantifying-the-cost-of-lea.tldr: CLQ measures the largest increase in average queue length caused by learning unknown system parameters.

paragraphs: Network embeddings commonly learn by making positively sampled node pairs more similar and negatively sampled pairs less similar. Yet successful sampling strategies can seem contradictory: some treat distant nodes as positive examples, while others include nearby nodes among negative examples. This paper investigates the relationship between these choices instead of assuming one proximity-based rule fits every purpose.

The analysis identifies two desired embedding properties, discrimination and monotonicity, and quantifies the empirical error of learned similarity scores relative to the sampling strategy. It finds that, in real-world applications, both properties cannot be satisfied simultaneously for every node pair. This establishes a tradeoff behind apparently competing sampling recommendations.

Guided by that tradeoff, the authors propose SENSEI. It satisfies discrimination while targeting partial monotonicity within the top-K ranking list, narrowing where the ordering requirement must hold. Extensive experiments show improvements over state-of-the-art plain network-embedding methods. The approach illustrates how analyzing incompatible objectives can motivate a more focused learning target and a practical embedding method.
neurips-2023-reconciling-competing-sampl.tldr: SENSEI resolves a sampling tradeoff by preserving discrimination while enforcing partial monotonicity within top-K rankings.

paragraphs: An agent that learns from images must cope with visual observations that differ from those encountered during training. Evaluating this ability is difficult when benchmarks cover only isolated tasks or a narrow category of change. RL-ViGen addresses that evaluation problem by bringing diverse tasks and a broad range of generalization types into one benchmark.

The paper also incorporates recent visual reinforcement-learning algorithms into a unified framework. This gives researchers a shared setting for comparing methods across multiple challenges. The purpose is to support conclusions about visual generalization that are less dependent on the particular task or category chosen for an evaluation.

The experiments find that no single evaluated algorithm dominates across all tasks. This result shows why strong performance on one benchmark setting should not be treated as evidence of universal visual robustness. RL-ViGen’s contribution is the broader testing foundation itself, together with implemented algorithms, intended to support research toward agents that generalize across more varied visual situations.
neurips-2023-rl-vigen-a-reinforcement-le.tldr: RL-ViGen broadens visual reinforcement-learning evaluation and finds that no tested algorithm dominates across all tasks.

paragraphs: Explaining a graph neural network requires accounting for how connected features interact, not merely identifying isolated important elements. SAME produces explanations after training, without retraining the predictive model. Its goal is to identify multiple connected graph pieces whose combined contribution helps explain the model’s behavior.

The method uses expansion-based Monte Carlo tree search to explore connected substructures at different scales. It then optimizes combinations of distinct substructures so the resulting explanation captures informative graph properties. Shapley-based reasoning guides its treatment of feature interactions, connecting the search for useful pieces with a principled notion of fair contribution.

The authors argue that this treatment has the potential to match the explanatory quality of a theoretically optimal Shapley explanation within polynomial time; this is not stated as an unconditional equivalence. Experiments report higher fidelity than previous leading methods across six real-world and synthetic benchmarks under matched testing conditions. The findings support considering several interacting graph pieces when seeking explanations that reflect a model’s predictions.
neurips-2023-same-uncovering-gnn-black-b.tldr: SAME explains graph neural networks through combinations of connected substructures, using Shapley-based interactions to guide informative explanations.

paragraphs: Federated learning combines contributions from multiple participants, creating a need to assess how much each participant helps. Such assessments can inform incentives, robustness measures, and client selection. Existing approaches often rely on Shapley values, but computing these values remains expensive even when techniques reconstruct models or skip unnecessary evaluations.

SPACE reduces this evaluation burden through two components: Federated Knowledge Amalgamation and Prototype-based Model Evaluation. Together, they enable participant evaluation within a single communication round and remove dependence on validation-set size from the evaluation effort. The approach targets the cost of contribution assessment itself, making it easier to use those assessments in subsequent federated-learning decisions.

Experiments show that SPACE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in running time and Pearson correlation coefficient, the reported correlation measure for the evaluation. Further experiments on client reweighting and selection demonstrate practical effectiveness. These findings connect faster assessment with useful downstream decisions, rather than presenting computational savings as the only benefit of the proposed method.
neurips-2023-space-single-round-particip.tldr: SPACE evaluates federated-learning participants in one communication round while improving reported runtime and correlation over leading methods.

paragraphs: Dynamic graphs can change in ways that undermine predictions learned from earlier data. This paper identifies cases where distribution shifts are not observable in the time domain but become visible in the spectral domain. That observation motivates examining frequency components of graph evolution rather than relying exclusively on time-domain analysis.

SILD applies a Fourier transform to trajectories of local graph neighborhoods, separating mixed dynamics into frequency components. A learned spectrum mask then distinguishes patterns that remain invariant from those that vary. Finally, invariant spectral filtering encourages the predictor to rely on the stable patterns when making predictions under distribution shifts.

The approach addresses both extracting useful spectral patterns and deciding which patterns should guide generalization. Experiments on synthetic and real-world dynamic graphs show superior performance for node classification and link prediction under distribution shifts. The findings support spectral analysis as a complementary way to expose changes that time-domain approaches can miss and to identify more stable predictive structure.
neurips-2023-spectral-invariant-learning.tldr: SILD separates dynamic-graph frequency patterns and emphasizes invariant ones to improve prediction under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Source-free adaptation must transfer a segmentation model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing its original training data. Updating the entire network is parameter-intensive, but ordinary visual prompts are not well suited to this setting: they can struggle to capture useful segmentation knowledge and often depend on labeled examples.

Uni-UVPT keeps the pretrained transformer backbone frozen and divides it into stages. A lightweight prompt adapter progressively encodes information into prompts between those stages, aiming to improve target-domain feature generalization. The framework also corrects pseudo-labels adaptively and uses consistency across multiple scales to reduce the influence of noisy labels and improve responses to spatial perturbations.

Experiments achieve state-of-the-art results on GTA5-to-Cityscapes and SYNTHIA-to-Cityscapes adaptation. The framework applies to various transformer backbones, supporting its use as a parameter-efficient approach to unsupervised knowledge transfer. Its central contribution is the combination of staged prompt adaptation and mechanisms for learning from unreliable target-domain supervision while the backbone remains fixed.
neurips-2023-when-visual-prompt-tuning-m.tldr: Uni-UVPT adapts frozen transformer segmentation models using staged prompts, pseudo-label correction, and multiscale consistency.

paragraphs: Predicting an intervention’s effect on a particular individual is difficult when that intervention has no historical recipient data. Conventional methods typically focus on interventions already observed. This paper studies zero-shot causal learning: estimating personalized effects for new interventions, including ones that did not exist when the model was trained.

CaML treats prediction of each intervention’s personalized effect as a separate learning task. It trains one meta-model across thousands of tasks constructed by sampling an intervention, people who received it, and people who did not. The model combines information about interventions with individual features, allowing predictions to draw on patterns learned across earlier tasks.

Experiments use large-scale medical claims and cell-line perturbation datasets. In these evaluations, CaML’s zero-shot predictions outperform strong baselines that were trained directly on data from the test interventions. This is an empirical result for the studied settings. It supports the possibility that shared learning across many interventions can provide useful predictive information even before outcomes from a new intervention are available.
neurips-2023-zero-shot-causal-learning-c.tldr: CaML learns across intervention-specific tasks to predict personalized effects of new interventions without training on their outcomes.
